extracted.subtask_description: Advice for composing a standout book query letter to send to literary agents or publishers, covering structure, tone, market positioning, and submission strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query letter length and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A query letter is a one page, 300-500 word, three to five paragraph letter that explains the premise of your book, including the main themes, important plot points, and the characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep to one page / ~300–500 words and three–five paragraphs. Include title and word count (see other entries). Agents typically spend about 10 seconds on each query, so brevity and clear structure matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do your research / target the right agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Before writing, make sure you know everything you can about the agent: that they represent your genre and are taking new authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research agents using resources like Manuscript Wish List and Publisher’s Marketplace. Look at an agent’s website and submission guidelines; researching shows you’ve done your homework and avoids wasted queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission guidelines exactly
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the agent’s website for submission instructions and do exactly as they ask.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission guideline adherence is essential — failure to follow stated requirements can disqualify your query before it’s read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with a great hook in the opening sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: The very first sentence about your book should hook the reader; agents spend about 10 seconds and often have assistants screen queries first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with a pivotal scene or a fascinating fact related to the story. If you have a personal connection or referral, briefly mention it in the opening. Also include the book title and word count in this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synopsis that leaves them wanting more
rubrics_metrics.description: The second paragraph should be a crisp synopsis—like back-cover copy—covering major themes, plot points, and a few words about the characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use crisp, tight, purposeful sentences; make sure every word is necessary. The goal is to leave the reader wondering how the book unfolds so they will request the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match the tone of your manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: The tone of your query letter should match the tone and voice of your book so the agent knows what to expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the query in the same voice/style as the manuscript—voice is especially important for nonfiction. Example: a light-hearted memoir should have a light query voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market positioning: include comparable titles (comps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help an agent envision where your book might sit on the shelf by including two similar books (comps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include two similar books that have been published in the last two years to demonstrate marketability and positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author bio and platform in closing
rubrics_metrics.description: The closing paragraph should be about you: a professional bio that includes previously published work, awards, and appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position yourself as an expert on your topic and show an author platform. 'Sing your own praises' — don’t be shy about relevant credentials and publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make clear why the book is unique and why you are qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: A query should answer: Why is my book unique? Why am I qualified to write this book?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly communicate the book’s unique selling points and your qualifications or authority to write it (experience, publications, expertise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and precision of prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Use crisp, tight, and purposeful sentences; ensure each word needs to be there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim unnecessary language; because queries are read quickly, every word must pull its weight. Write like back-cover copy for the synopsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and iterative revision after rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Querying is a long game; expect rejection and continue revising and sending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you’ve sent at least 10 queries without requests, go back to the drawing board and rework your letter. Patience and revision are key to eventual success.
